On the big N or NW swells that light it up, it stacks giant righthanders around the west side of the island and careens them down along the southern edge of the headland. It faces open ocean and pulls in energy from both the North and South Pacific, so there's swell potential across autumn, winter, spring, and summer. It only breaks a few times a year, but when it does it throws wedgy, open-face rights that funnel for hundreds of yards, along with steep, lined-up lefts that can barrel when there is enough west in the swell.
